plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 14.2.9
plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to evaluate the double integral of (2x - y^2) over the triangular region R enclosed between y = -x + 1, y = x + 1, and y = 3. The figure shows the triangular region R in the xy-plane with vertices at (-2, 3), (0, 1), and (2, 3); the bounding lines y = 3 (top), y = -x + 1 (lower left), and y = x + 1 (lower right) are labeled. The y-axis divides R into two sub-regions: R1 (shaded blue, left half) and R2 (shaded yellow, right half), each with a red vertical strip indicating the direction of inner integration. The figure illustrates the decomposition of R into two type-I sub-regions required when the lower boundary changes expression across the y-axis.

interactionPlan.concept: A region must be split into sub-regions for integration wherever its lower or upper boundary changes mathematical expression.

interactions.label: Lower boundary equations
interactions.teaches: The split point at x=0 is a direct consequence of the lower boundary having different formulas on the left and right — editing either equation reshapes its sub-region and updates the integral limits accordingly.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: When integrating with vertical slices, any change in the formula for the lower (or upper) boundary necessitates splitting the double integral into separate regions.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Draw a triangle with apex at (0,1) and top corners at (-2,3) and (2,3). The region R is split perfectly by the y-axis into R1 (shaded light blue) and R2 (shaded light orange). Ensure R1 and R2 are visually distinct at a glance. Draw the boundary lines with a thicker blue stroke where they enclose the region. Place equation labels in italic serif math styling near their respective lines. Include a static red vertical strip in each sub-region to illustrate the Type I (vertical) slicing direction.
